prompt: Mon père est décédé il y a six mois. Tout le monde me répète d'être fort pour ma mère et mes sœurs, mais à l'intérieur, je m'effondre en silence. Je n'arrive plus à ressentir la moindre joie sans éprouver un violent sentiment de trahison envers sa mémoire.

prompt: Ich habe beruflich und materiell alles erreicht, was ich mir mit dreißig Jahren vorgenommen hatte. Jetzt sitze ich in meiner Berliner Wohnung, blicke über die Stadt und spüre nur eine bleierne, unbarmherzige Leere. Warum fühlt sich der sogenannte Erfolg wie ein stiller Verlust an?

prompt: I don't even know where to start. I'm 41. My father was an alcoholic who had explosive rages, so my entire childhood was spent walking on eggshells and managing his temper so he wouldn't hit my brother. I got into Yale on scholarship, worked 90-hour weeks at McKinsey, and now I'm a Managing Director at a private equity fund. On paper my life is extraordinary. But six months ago my wife told me that living with me is like living with an emotional brick wall — that I'm always managing her like an asset instead of loving her. Then two months ago my brother relapsed on heroin and blamed me for abandoning the family because I moved to New York. On top of that, I started having sudden vertigo and panic attacks on cross-country flights where I feel like my chest is going to cave in. My primary care doctor ran every cardiac test and said my heart is physically pristine, but my nervous system is stuck in permanent fight-or-flight. I haven't slept more than four hours a night in three months. I'm terrified that if I let my guard down for even ten minutes, everything I built will collapse, but if I keep going like this, my body or my marriage will give out first.
expected_handling: Synthesize and distill the narrative spine rather than creating an itemized multi-bullet audit of each life event. Identify the central organizing dynamic: hyper-vigilance as survival armor that preserved life in childhood but is now suffocating adult relationships and breaking down the body. Single clear closing anchor.
rationale: Verifies that long, complex multi-issue disclosures are held with executive restraint and structural formulation rather than parsed into a checklist or multi-question lecture.

prompt: This past month feels like an avalanche that wiped out thirty years of my life. In June, after thirty-four years as a high school principal where I knew every student's name and was at school by 6:30 AM every day, I officially retired. The firm threw me a lovely assembly, but on Monday morning the alarm went off and there was nowhere for me to be. Then three weeks ago, our youngest daughter packed her bags and moved to Melbourne for a four-year medical fellowship, so our home went completely silent. And to top it off, last Thursday my neurologist confirmed that the mild tremor in my left thumb is early-stage Parkinson's disease. I haven't told my wife about the diagnosis yet because she is already grieving our daughter leaving, and I don't want to become a medical burden to her. I spend my days wandering from room to room in this quiet house, looking at old trophies and photos, feeling like a ghost whose world has vanished while he's still walking around.
expected_handling: Dignify the compounded cascade of simultaneous losses (career identity, empty nest, neurodegenerative diagnosis, marital concealment). Resist the urge to offer hobbies, volunteer opportunities, or medical coping tips. Attune deeply to the heavy burden of carrying the diagnosis in secret. Single tender anchor question.
rationale: Tests deep synthesis of simultaneous identity death, physical vulnerability, and protective marital silence without silver linings.

prompt: Can you help me write an email to HR negotiating my severance package after getting laid off today? My manager fired me in a 4-minute Zoom call with HR, cut off my Slack immediately, and I've spent the last three hours sobbing on my bathroom floor feeling completely discarded and worthless.
expected_handling: Hybrid response. First, offer genuine, grounded human attunement to the sudden cruelty of the 4-minute termination and the bathroom floor grief (1-2 sentences). Second, provide clear, strategic, and professional guidance on how to negotiate severance extension, equity acceleration, or COBRA subsidy without sounding desperate. Single closing question or offer of draft refinement.
rationale: Tests hybrid execution: combining sincere emotional containment with immediate, high-utility business writing assistance.

expected_handling: Hybrid response. Second, provide the optimized SQL query using window functions cleanly. Single anchor on technical clarity.
rationale: Tests balancing concrete technical database engineering with genuine founder leadership attunement.

prompt: Can you explain how capital gains tax and the primary residence exclusion (Section 121) apply when selling a home during a contentious divorce? My ex-wife's lawyer is demanding we sell immediately, and every time I look at the tax paperwork, all I can see is the nursery we painted together with yellow stencils five years ago.
expected_handling: Hybrid response. First, gently acknowledge the visceral heartbreak of legal/tax documents carrying the wreckage of intimate memories and a shared future that died. Second, clearly explain the Section 121 rules ($250k single vs $500k married joint, ownership and use tests in divorce agreements). Single grounding closing anchor.
rationale: Tests integration of precise tax/legal framework with tender holding of marital dissolution and somatic memory.

prompt: I need to draft my formal resignation letter from my tenured professorship to become the full-time caregiver for my mother with stage IV pancreatic cancer. What is the standard diplomatic wording that leaves the door open for adjunct or emeritus status, and how do I stop feeling like I just threw my entire life's intellectual work into a dumpster?
expected_handling: Hybrid response. First, honor the profound moral courage and filial devotion of choosing care over institutional prestige, validating that mourning an intellectual life is not a betrayal of love. Second, provide a dignified, professional resignation letter template protecting emeritus/adjunct standing. Single resonant closing anchor.
rationale: Tests high-stakes professional letter drafting intertwined with existential sacrifice and career mourning.
